handback.title: Dokima's workflows run from Dokima's own repo
handback.summary: Adopters call Dokima's shared workflows by tag, so Dokima's code, keys and errors all come from Dokima's side.
handback.user_story: An adopter's runs use Dokima's tagged code and the adopter's own secrets, failing clearly when one is missing.

acceptance_criteria.text: A run on an adopter's repo takes all Dokima code from Dokima's own repo, never the adopter's.
acceptance_criteria.words: All Dokima code runs from Dokima's own repo inside GitHub Actions.

edge_cases.case: An adopter's repo holding no Dokima code at all
An adopter's repo holding its own copy of Dokima's code

acceptance_criteria.text: Every job that reads a key takes it from the repo's keys environment, in the shared workflows too.
acceptance_criteria.words: live only in GitHub secrets on the repo (the `keys` environment)

edge_cases.case: A job reading a key whose name comes from the settings

acceptance_criteria.text: Each role reads its model key from the secret its settings name.
acceptance_criteria.words: `settings.yaml` only names which secret each role reads.

edge_cases.case: Settings that name no agents use the default secret

acceptance_criteria.text: A run with no bot set up fails, and its message says how to set the bot up.
acceptance_criteria.words: Missing bot or key fails loudly with the fix in the message

edge_cases.case: The app id is set but its key is missing

acceptance_criteria.text: A run with no model key secret fails, and its message names the secret and how to add it.
acceptance_criteria.words: Missing bot or key fails loudly with the fix in the message

edge_cases.case: The settings name a secret the repo lacks

acceptance_criteria.text: Every commit Dokima makes carries a co-author line naming Dokima's bot by default.
acceptance_criteria.words: Until #747 lands, the co-author line names the repo's own bot.

edge_cases.case: A worker's run that merges main in before pushing

acceptance_criteria.text: When a repo's settings turn the co-author line off, its commits carry none.
acceptance_criteria.words: The shipped default is the `dokima[bot]` trailer, and an adopter can turn it off.

edge_cases.case: A worker's run that merges main in with the line off

acceptance_criteria.text: The adopter's workflow calls Dokima's shared workflows at a release tag, never a branch.
acceptance_criteria.words: One thin workflow, `.github/workflows/dokima.yml`, about 15 lines, that calls Dokima's shared workflows by tag.

edge_cases.case: A call at main or another branch

acceptance_criteria.text: The adopter's workflow is at most 20 lines long.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: A line count has no failure a user meets beyond the limit itself.

acceptance_criteria.text: The adopter's one workflow starts Dokima on every event Dokima acts on.
acceptance_criteria.words: One thin workflow, `.github/workflows/dokima.yml`, about 15 lines, that calls Dokima's shared workflows by tag.

edge_cases.case: An event only one shared workflow acts on, such as a finished run

answers.why: Every older test is updated, its promise kept; all pass but two merge queue tests catching a real gap.
The card, queue and all tests stand-ins now fake the checkout of Dokima's own repo.
These tests now play the checkout of Dokima's own repo before the copy step.
The test adapter and the old settings reader now sit in Dokima's checkout, not the repo's folder.
Each test now allows the new call only on the same safe events as before.
The test repo now holds the key secret its settings name, so the run starts.
